title: Soften People's Resistance by Confirming Their Self-Opinion: The Law of Defensiveness
coreMove: Lower ego threat by affirming the person's chosen self-image before introducing the change they would otherwise defend against.
sourcePressure: This law turns persuasion into ego management: direct identity threat produces resistance, so influence starts by confirming self-opinion before asking for movement.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating this as flattery or soft wording instead of removing the identity threat that blocks truth.

exampleSpecs.domain: a fire marshal correcting a beloved diner owner about blocked exits
exampleSpecs.audience: a regulator who needs compliance without triggering pride
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a safety fix happens before inspection fines
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the marshal starts by naming the owner's care for regulars, then points to the blocked exit as the one thing betraying that care
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a red exit sign half-hidden behind stacked syrup boxes

exampleSpecs.domain: a podcast producer telling a famous host to stop interrupting guests
exampleSpecs.audience: a producer managing a talent's identity as generous and sharp
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether interviews keep losing the best answers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she plays the host a clip where his curiosity is visible, then shows the interruption that prevents the guest from rewarding that curiosity
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a waveform on an audio screen with one spike circled

exampleSpecs.domain: a synagogue committee asking a longtime treasurer to adopt new controls
exampleSpecs.audience: a committee chair avoiding an insult to trustworthiness
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether financial safeguards pass or stall in wounded pride
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chair frames the controls as a way to protect the treasurer's reputation after years of service, not as suspicion
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a locked cashbox beside a typed donation ledger

exampleSpecs.domain: a wildlife rehab trainer correcting a volunteer who handles birds too confidently
exampleSpecs.audience: a trainer turning confidence toward care
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether an injured hawk is stressed by ego-driven handling
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the trainer praises the volunteer's steadiness, then says true steadiness means moving slower than confidence wants
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a leather falconry glove resting beside a carrier crate

exampleSpecs.domain: a coding bootcamp mentor telling an advanced student to write simpler code
exampleSpecs.audience: a mentor whose correction threatens the student's identity as talented
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the mentor predicts the student will resist simplicity, then frames simple code as the mark of someone ready for teammates
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pull request page filled with nested functions

exampleSpecs.domain: a tenant organizer asking a proud landlord to repair a stairwell
exampleSpecs.audience: an organizer trying to avoid a public shaming spiral
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether repairs happen without hardening both sides
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she opens by naming the landlord's pride in keeping the building family-run, then connects the loose stair tread to that promise
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a brass apartment number plate beside a loose stair tread

skillTargets: separate genuine confirmation from empty praise

tryThisNowSpec: Before correcting someone, name the identity they are trying to protect in one clean sentence, then make the request fit that identity.

sourceAnchors.name: Lyndon B. Johnson
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses Johnson to show influence built on reading what people need to feel about themselves before asking them to move
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Johnson's influence starts with the other person's self-opinion, not with the argument he wants to win.
